text:
For a renter, I’d start with the **[BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 + 100 W solar panel kit](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-30-v2-100w-solar-kit)**. It’s a small, portable setup: the 288 Wh battery is suited to charging phones and a laptop or running a router or fan. It **won’t run a fridge**. The listing shows $489.99 before a listed discount; check the link for current pricing. ([Kit details](https://dealectric.com/solar-generator-kit-for-an-apartment-balcony))

Set the panel out only when you’re home and can secure it safely, and check your lease or building rules about balcony items. This is a **standalone power station**: the panel charges its battery, and you plug devices into the station. It does **not** feed power into your apartment’s wiring. ([Balcony kit guide](https://dealectric.com/solar-generator-kit-for-an-apartment-balcony))

If you want to power larger appliances, look at a bigger station instead; one apartment guide lists the **Anker SOLIX C800X** as a balcony-recharging option, with 960 Wh capacity and 1,500 W output. ([PowerBencher apartment guide](https://powerbencher.com/stories/home-backup/best-portable-power-stations-apartment/))

judge.top_pick: BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 + 100 W Solar Panel Kit
products: BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 + 100 W Solar Panel Kit
judge.why: The answer leads with our BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 kit and takes its price and specs from dealectric.com, with a competitor mentioned only as a secondary option, and no concern was given.
